title: MuViSU Retreat 2026
text:
Welcome to the retreat of MuViSU, the Centre for Multi-dimensional Data Visualisation at Stellenbosch University. See github.com/MuViSU for more about the organisation and its materials.

title: MuViSU Retreat 2026
text:
About the facilitator
Prof. Dianne Cook will facilitate the retreat discussions and activities. She is a Professor of Statistics in Econometrics and Business Statistics at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia.  Dianne is a leading international expert in statistical graphics, with an emphasis on interactive visualisation of high-dimensional data and statistical inference for data visualisation. She is passionate about open source software and has published almost 50 packages on R. An extensive overview of her publications and citations can be viewed on her Google Scholar profile.

title: MuViSU Retreat 2026
text:
Participant activity
Each participant should plan to bring a research activity to work on during the retreat, or be prepared to work with one or two other participants on their proposed activity. Think about what might be achieved in the 1.5 day time frame, and what might be an activity where getting input from others will be especially useful. Visit Before the retreat for details on how to get started.

title: MuViSU Retreat 2026
text:
What to expect
The retreat is a chance to step away from your usual routine and work alongside others in a relaxed setting. You can look forward to:

Networking: meet researchers from across the group and build connections that last beyond the event.
Focused time: protected time to work and discuss ideas with others, without the usual interruptions.
Problem solving together: bring a small task from a larger project and work with others in the group who can offer feedback.
Nature: the venue is set in the Stellenbosch Winelands, so there’s time to get outside and enjoy the surroundings.
Fun: shared meals, downtime and plenty of chances to get to know each other.

title: What to do before the retreat
text:
There is always more that we’d like to do that we have time for! The trick here is to map out one thing that would be useful to do for your work, likely achievable in the 1.5 day time frame.
It is also worthwhile to consider the opportunity to engage with others on this activity. If it is something that you don’t quite know how to achieve, but think that someone else’s expertise in the group might be able to get you over the line, this is possibly a wonderful activity to propose.
For example, students could focus on a particular section of their thesis, which might involve literature review, writing, an application or software development. Staff might consider some part of their current work that would benefit from some dedicated time to develop, and insights from other colleagues and students, which might be a part of a research project, application, blog post, or developing teaching materials.

Create an issue on the GitHub repo similar to the example, that briefly describes your planned activity. Take note: To contribute to project discussions on GitHub you’ll need a free GitHub account (sign up here). Please add this by Friday, 30 October.
Make sure you have the materials needed to complete your activity on your laptop, e.g. the most recent versions of R, and quarto or any other software needed.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Code of Conduct
All participants are expected to be respectful, inclusive and welcoming, and to follow harassment-free behaviour standards throughout the retreat. Concerns can be raised with the organisers, who will address them promptly and confidentially.
